test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Tsangpo and Dihang are other names of which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Yarlung Tsangpo**, commonly known as **the Yarlung Zangbo**, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River in** China's Tibet Autonomous Region**.
 
• It is** Tibet's longest river and China's sixth-longest river**.
 
• The top section is also known as **Dangque Zangbu**, which translates to** "Horse River."**
 
• It begins at the Angsi Glacier in western Tibet, southeast of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar, and flows through the South Tibet Valley and the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon before entering Arunachal Pradesh, India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Brahmaputra** is a transboundary river that flows through **Tibet, China, India, and Bangladesh**.
 
• It is also known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang/Dihang River in Arunachal Pradesh, and Luit in Assamese.
 
• It is also known as the Tsangpo-Brahmaputra and the Indian Red River (when referring to the whole river including the stretch within the Tibet Autonomous Region).
 
• It has the ninth biggest discharge and is the 15th longest river in the world. 
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo River originates in the Manasarovar Lake region, near Mount Kailash, on the northern side of the Himalayas in Burang County, Tibet, and flows through southern Tibet, breaking through the Himalayas in great gorges (including the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon), and into Arunachal Pradesh.
